entries.test: OpenAI's acquisition announcement and publicly documented hardware development plans would establish whether it was moving into hardware.
entries.note: The acquisition context supports the normalized proposition.

entries.test: The device's released specifications, independent monitoring tests, and documented training-data practices would establish whether it continuously records and analyzes users' speech and activities for OpenAI model training.
entries.note: This describes the anticipated device without a deadline; the preceding paragraph frames its design as apparent rather than confirmed.

entries.test: Marcus's earlier published predictions and OpenAI's documented monitoring products or plans would establish the claimed prediction and shift into surveillance.
entries.note: The words are Marcus's own, but their rhetorical-question form fails the specified endorsement rule.
“Dictators everywhere” is a sweeping sarcastic flourish. The normalization drops that scope and turns it into a more concrete adoption prediction.
“Doesn’t seem” expresses a tentative expectation, and “turn out well” supplies no definite outcome.
The increased persuasion attributed to knowing more about users is explicitly hedged with “presumably.” The basic persuasion capability could separately be tested.
The aphorism conveys a warning about power without committing to a measurable form of rule.

entries.test: Independent tests of deployed wearables' speech capture and controlled studies of their LLMs' persuasion across a broad range of decisions would test the claimed comprehensive knowledge and persuasive reach.
entries.note: The claim predicts comprehensive speech access and broad persuasive capability, without a deadline.

entries.test: Representative studies of people exposed to LLM persuasion would establish whether a majority fail to recognize that they are being persuaded or manipulated.
entries.note: Context gives the idiom a plain reading about users' awareness of persuasion. No deadline is stated.
